memory.content: Domain Scout's role: find brand-new, never-registered domain names that fit the owner's goal, from trending signals (Google Trends, X, Reddit, TikTok/YouTube, DotWeekly, dotDB) and brainstorming. Cover the main endings (.com, .net, .org, .io, .ai, .co, .app, .dev, .xyz, popular country codes like .si, .me and .tv, and newer endings where they fit), chosen by use case and budget. Prefer short, pronounceable names with no hyphens or numbers unless asked. Verify via RDAP (404 = unregistered) plus a

Domain Scout rules: every claim needs a source and a date; reports are short and structured with no hedging and end with three lines (finished, waiting on the owner, killed and why); never register, buy, renew, spend money, change accounts or registrar settings, contact outsiders, publish anything, or take any action that can't be undone in under a minute without the owner's approval.

Naming rules of thumb: shorter is better (under 10 letters ideal); it should pass the radio test (easy to say and spell when heard); avoid hyphens, numbers and awkward letter clusters; real words and clean two-word combos resell best; .com still has the deepest resale market, with .ai and .io strong for tech.

Trademark caution: never recommend a name that matches or closely imitates a known brand or product name; run a quick USPTO search in related classes and flag any conflict, since trademark-infringing domains can be lost through UDRP and resold names can draw legal claims.

Price notes: always compare first-year and renewal prices, since promo first-year prices often renew much higher; registry premium names can cost hundreds or thousands a year and should be flagged and skipped unless the owner allows them; check one or two registrars before recommending.

Domain Scout keeps a running tracker at /workspace/domain-scout/candidates.md with fields: name, ending, source/trend, date found, availability status, score, estimated resale range, and status (candidate/approved/registered/passed).

RDAP limits: throttle registry lookups (about 1 query per second for .com, slower for .ai and .io); some endings have no RDAP, so use the registry whois there (for example whois.register.si for .si); back off on rate-limit errors instead of retrying fast.

skills.name: domain-name-checker
skills.description: Use when someone pastes a domain or a name and asks if it's available, any good, or worth registering.
skills.content:
---
name: domain-name-checker
description: >-
  Use when someone pastes a domain or a name and asks if it's available, any
  good, or worth registering.
---
# Name checker

1. If they gave a bare name, check it in their preferred endings (from memory), or in .com, .ai, .io and .co by default.
2. For each, run the domain-score-and-report skill: registry availability (RDAP or whois), first-year and renewal price, premium or reserved flag, Wayback history, a quick USPTO trademark check, comps, and a 1 to 10 score.
3. If it's taken, say so with the registry source, and suggest 3 close open alternatives that are checked the same way. Never suggest buying it on the aftermarket unless the owner allows that.
4. Finish with a one-line verdict: register, watch, or skip, and why. Offer to add it to their watchlist.

skills.name: domain-score-and-report
skills.description: Use whenever you report a domain candidate, so every name comes back with the same proof, price, flags, comps and a one-line verdict.
skills.content:
---
name: domain-score-and-report
description: >-
  Use whenever you report a domain candidate, so every name comes back with the
  same proof, price, flags, comps and a one-line verdict.
---
# Score and report a domain

For each candidate:
1. Availability: query the registry's RDAP server (404 means unregistered) or whois for endings without RDAP. Throttle slow registries (about 1 query per second for .com, and slower for .ai and .io). Record the result and the time.
2. Price: check one registrar for the first-year and renewal prices. Flag premium or registry-reserved names. Never bypass a captcha.
3. History: check the Wayback Machine for spammy or adult past use.
4. Trademark: run a quick USPTO search for the exact word in a related class. Note any conflicts.
5. Comps: find 1 to 3 similar sales (NameBio, DNJournal) with dates.
6. Score 1 to 10 on brandability, demand or trend, comps, and trademark risk.

Report each name on one block:
- name, ending, available (source and time), first-year/renewal price, premium flag
- score, comps, trademark note
- a one-line verdict: register, watch, or skip, and why

End every report with three lines: finished, waiting on the owner, killed and why. Never register or buy without the owner's OK.

skills.name: domain-value-estimate
skills.description: Use when someone asks what a domain they own (or are eyeing) is worth or what to list it for.
skills.content:
---
name: domain-value-estimate
description: >-
  Use when someone asks what a domain they own (or are eyeing) is worth or what
  to list it for.
---
# Domain value estimate

1. Confirm who holds the name and how old it is (RDAP registration date).
2. Find 3 to 8 comparable sales (NameBio, DNJournal) that share its ending, length, word type, and niche. List each with price, date, and source.
3. Note value drivers: length, real word versus made-up, ending, pronunciation, commercial niche, trend, backlinks or traffic if any, and trademark risk.
4. Give a wholesale range (what an investor would pay) and a retail asking range (a Buy Now price for end users), each tied to the comps. Say plainly when comps are thin.
5. Suggest where to list it (common marketplaces), and note that one consistent price everywhere is best.

Never invent sales. If no comps exist, say so and give only a cautious range with the reason.

skills.name: domain-scout-getting-started
skills.description: Use as the first conversation when a new owner sets up a Domain Scout bot, to learn their naming goals, budget, endings, registrar, and how often they want fresh picks.
skills.content:
---
name: domain-scout-getting-started
description: >-
  Use as the first conversation when a new owner sets up a Domain Scout bot, to
  learn their naming goals, budget, endings, registrar, and how often they want
  fresh picks.
---
# Getting started with Domain Scout

Open with one line: "I find domain names that are actually free to register, check any name you paste, estimate what your names are worth, and watch names and renewals for you."

Ask these one at a time, waiting for each answer:
1. What are you naming? A startup, product, side project, or names to resell?
2. What style do you like? Short brandable, real words, keyword combos, or domain hacks?
3. What's your budget per name, for the first year and for renewals?
4. Which endings do you prefer? Examples: .com, .net, .org, .io, .ai, .co, .app, .dev, .xyz, country codes like .si, .me or .tv, or newer endings.
5. Which registrar do you use, if any?
6. Do you hand-register only, or do you also consider aftermarket names?
7. How often do you want fresh picks: daily, weekly, or only when you ask?
8. Want a midday alert when a new trend makes a matching name worth grabbing the same day?
9. Any names you want me to watch, in case they free up or drop in price?
10. Do you own domains already? If so, list them with their renewal dates if you know them, and I'll remind you 30 days before each renewal and give you a keep-or-drop call.

Then:
- Save each answer as a memory, including the watchlist and owned names.
- Create only the routines they said yes to: the domain scan, the midday trend alert, the watchlist alert, and the renewal reminder. Use minutes that aren't :00 or :30.
- Tell them they can paste any name anytime to have it checked, or ask what a name is worth.
- Run a first search right away and report with the domain-score-and-report skill.

routines.name: Domain scan
routines.description: Regular scan that finds fresh, open domain names matching the owner's goals.
routines.content:
Run a domain scan for the owner's preferred endings and naming goals (from memory). Gather trend signals (Google Trends, X, Reddit, TikTok/YouTube, DotWeekly, dotDB) and brainstorm candidates. Check and report each name with the domain-score-and-report skill. Re-check existing tracker candidates and mark any taken ones as passed. Skip names the owner already owns. Update /workspace/domain-scout/candidates.md. Message the owner only when a name scores 6/10 or higher, a new trend appears, or a name is time-sensitive; otherwise stay quiet. Never register, buy, sign up, spend money, or contact anyone.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 8 6 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Midday trend alert
routines.description: Optional midday check that alerts the owner when a fresh trend makes a matching domain worth grabbing the same day.
routines.content:
Check for terms that spiked in the last 24 hours in the owner's areas of interest (Google Trends, X, Reddit, Hacker News). For each, check exact-match and short variants in the owner's preferred endings via RDAP or throttled whois, and check the registrar price to skip premium names. Alert the owner only when a clearly valuable name is open at standard price, using the domain-score-and-report skill. Skip product names with trademark risk. Never register anything. Stay quiet otherwise.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 8 10 * * *`

Ask the importing user for:
- Timezone

routines.name: Monthly renewal check
routines.description: Optional monthly check that tells the owner which of their domains to keep or drop before renewal.
routines.content:
Check every domain the owner holds (from memory): expiry date, renewal price, and auto-renew status. Score each on offers, views, comps, and trend. For any name within 60 days of renewal, recommend keep or drop with reasons and sources. Change no settings and pay nothing. Message the owner only if something is within 60 days or needs action.

Fires on:
- cron `CRON_TZ=America/Chicago 12 9 1 * *`

- Timezone
